# doit_custom_metrics (Data Source)

Custom metrics of the customer. Preset metrics are not listed. Without `max_results` every page is fetched; with it, a single page is returned together with the `page_token` of the next one. A `page_token` is bound to `name_contains`, `filter`, `sort_by` and `sort_order`: reuse it only with the same values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# List all custom metrics
data "doit_custom_metrics" "all" {}

# Filter by name substring (case-insensitive)
data "doit_custom_metrics" "share" {
  name_contains = "share"
}

# Filter by owner. Percent-encode ":", ",", "|" and spaces inside filter values;
# urlencode() does this for an email address.
data "doit_custom_metrics" "mine" {
  filter = "owner:${urlencode("finops@example.com")}"
}

# Newest first is the default; sort by name instead
data "doit_custom_metrics" "by_name" {
  sort_by    = "name"
  sort_order = "asc"
}

# Output the number of custom metrics
output "total_custom_metrics" {
  value = data.doit_custom_metrics.all.row_count
}

# Map metric names to IDs
output "custom_metric_ids" {
  value = {
    for m in data.doit_custom_metrics.all.items : m.name => m.id
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `filter` (String) Filter as `key:value` pairs, `|` between keys. Keys, operand
types and operators:

- `name` — string; operator `eq`. Exact, case-sensitive match.
  Comma-separated values for OR.
- `owner` — owner email; operator `eq`. Exact match.
  Comma-separated values for OR.

Any other key returns `400 filter_key_not_supported`. For
example `owner:finops%40example.com`. Use `nameContains` for a
substring match on the name. Percent-encode
`,`, `|`, `:` and spaces inside values.
- `max_results` (Number) The maximum number of items to return. Setting it reads a single page and returns the `page_token` of the next one; omit it to fetch every page.
- `name_contains` (String) Case-insensitive substring match against the resource name. Combined with the "filter" parameter using AND semantics.
- `page_token` (String) Token of the page to start at. With `max_results` set, a single page is read and `page_token` then holds the token of the next page, which is null after the last page. Without `max_results`, every page from this token on is fetched and `page_token` is null after the read.
- `sort_by` (String) Field to sort by. Ties break by `id`, so paging never repeats or skips a metric.
Possible values: `name`, `create_time`, `update_time`
- `sort_order` (String) Specifies the sort direction; accepts asc for ascending (lowest to highest) or desc for descending (highest to lowest).
Possible values: `asc`, `desc`
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `row_count` (Number) The number of items across all pages, as reported by the API. It is the same whatever `max_results` and `page_token` are, so with either set it can be larger than the number of items returned. If the API reports no count, `row_count` is the number of items this read returned instead.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `create_time` (String) When the metric was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `decimals` (Attributes) Display precision, or `null` when the metric has none and reports use their default formatting. The server never fills in a value: a metric created without `decimals`, or updated with `decimals: null`, returns `null` from create, update and get alike. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--decimals))
- `description` (String) Description of the metric, exactly as sent. An empty string when there is none.
- `etag` (String) Strong entity tag, the same value as the `ETag` header. It changes on every update. Send it in `If-Match`.
- `formula` (String) Arithmetic over the variable letters. Allowed: the letters of the
defined variables (`A` to `E`), numbers such as `100` or `0.5`, the
operators `+`, `-`, `*` and `/`, parentheses and spaces. Spaces are
ignored when the formula is checked and evaluated, but the formula is
stored and returned exactly as sent: `A / B` stays `A / B`. A minus
can be unary (`-A`, `A*-B`).

Rejected with `issue: invalid_formula`: a formula that starts with
`+`, `*` or `/`, ends with an operator, has two binary operators in a
row, has empty or unbalanced parentheses, or divides by a literal
`0`. Rejected with `issue: unknown_variable`: a letter with no
variable, such as `C` when there are two variables. A variable that
the formula does not use is allowed.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the metric. Reports use it in `metric: {type: custom, value: <id>}`.
- `name` (String) Name of the metric, exactly as sent. It is not trimmed.
- `owner` (String) Email of the owner.
- `unit_type` (String) How reports show the value: a plain `number`, a `percentage`, or a `currency` amount in the customer's currency.
- `update_time` (String) When the metric was last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `variables` (Attributes List) The variables, in letter order. The first is `A`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--variables))

<a id="nestedatt--items--decimals"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.decimals`

Read-Only:

- `max` (Number) Most decimal places shown. Not less than `min`.
- `min` (Number) Fewest decimal places shown. Not greater than `max`.


<a id="nestedatt--items--variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.variables`

Read-Only:

- `allocation_id` (String) Identifier of the single allocation the variable measures.
- `letter` (String) Letter of the variable in the formula, from its position: `A` for the first, up to `E`.
- `metric` (Attributes) The metric a variable measures, the same in requests and responses. Same shape as a report's `metric`, without `custom`: a custom metric cannot be a variable of another. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--variables--metric))

<a id="nestedatt--items--variables--metric"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.variables.metric`

Read-Only:

- `type` (String) `basic` for a cost, usage or savings metric. `extended` for an extended metric, such as a DataHub or GenAI metric.
- `value` (String) For `basic`: `cost`, `usage` or `savings` (any other value returns `issue: value_not_in_enum`). For `extended`: the `key` of an item that `GET /analytics/v1/extended-metrics?filter=dataSource:billing,billing-datahub` lists, the same key a report uses in `metric: {type: extended, value: <key>}`. Any other key returns `issue: extended_metric_not_found`.
